extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (especially those applying to NINDS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how NIH (NINDS) applications are scored and percentiled, how preliminary and final impact scores are produced, and what information appears in the summary statement and when it is released.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH 9-point rating scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH uses a 9-point rating scale for all applications with a score of 1 meaning exceptional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score is the basic numeric measure of impact; it is applied to all applications reviewed under NIH procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned reviewers and preliminary impact scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed by at least 3 reviewers prior to the peer review meeting and each assigned reviewer provides a preliminary impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary impact scores help inform the committee on which applications are most meritorious and should be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion determines final overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussed applications will receive a final overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because discussing all applications is not always feasible, some applications may be not discussed and will not receive an overall impact score. The decision to discuss an application is informed by preliminary scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not discussed applications receive no overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Some applications may be not discussed and will not receive an overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not-discussed status affects whether an application gets a final overall impact score; applicants should be aware that absence of discussion means no overall score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile rank
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to your score, the percentile shows the ranking of your application relative to the other applications reviewed by that study section at its last three meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentiles provide a relative standing metric across applications within that study section over a defined recent window; note that not all applications are percentiled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which applications are percentiled vs not percentiled
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentiled: Applications reviewed and scored at CSR in a standing study section. Not percentiled: Applications reviewed and scored at NINDS; Applications reviewed and scored at CSR in a special emphasis panel. In some special case scenarios there are applications that are not percentiled in a CSR standing study section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an application receives a percentile depends on where and how it was reviewed (CSR standing study section vs CSR special emphasis panel vs NINDS-reviewed). To understand how NINDS will consider your score or percentile, consult the NINDS Paylines page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scientific Review Officer (SRO) prepares the summary statement for each application which contains a resume of the discussion (if discussed), the reviewers' critiques, the priority score, and budget and administrative notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement becomes the official Institute or Center record of the recommendations made by the peer review committee; it includes critiques and administrative notes useful for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of summary statement release
rubrics_metrics.description: SROs endeavor to get summary statements out to applicants as soon as possible. You can expect a summary statement to be released anytime between ~30 days after the meeting to 30 days before the Advisory Council meeting the application will be considered at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect this approximate window for receiving summary statements and plan follow-up (e.g., contacting Program Officer, revising if fixable) accordingly.
